title: iPhone Repairs in Burwood: Genuine vs Third-Party
meta_title: iPhone Repairs in Burwood: Parts Guide
meta_description: Choosing between genuine and third-party parts for an iPhone repair in Burwood? Here's what actually changes, and how to compare your repair options.
intro_html: Genuine Apple parts and quality third-party parts can both produce a solid iPhone repair, but genuine parts avoid on-screen warnings about non-Apple components and keep features like battery health reporting working exactly as Apple intends — which matters most if you plan to keep or resell the phone with its original specifications intact. Burwood, as one of New South Wales' largest cities, has a reasonable spread of Apple Store, Authorised Service Provider and independent options to choose between.
key_takeaways: Non-genuine screens or batteries can trigger an on-screen notice in iOS, though the phone will still function.
Battery health reporting can be affected by non-genuine batteries, making the percentage reading less reliable.
An Apple Store or Authorised Service Provider is the safest choice for in-warranty iPhones.
Independent repairers can be faster and more flexible for out-of-warranty repairs, often using quality aftermarket parts.
Turn off Find My iPhone before any repair so the device can be fully tested afterward.

sections.heading: What's different about repairing an iPhone specifically?
sections.html: Apple's software checks certain components, like the screen and battery, against the phone's internal records. If a non-genuine part is installed, iOS can display a notice noting that it can't verify the part is genuine — this doesn't stop the phone from working, but it's worth knowing about before you choose a repairer. Battery health reporting can also become less accurate with a non-genuine battery, since the percentage figure relies on calibration data tied to genuine Apple components.

sections.heading: Where you can get an iPhone repaired
sections.html: There are three broad options: an Apple Store, an Apple Authorised Service Provider, or an independent repairer. An Apple Store or Authorised Service Provider uses only genuine parts and preserves any remaining warranty or AppleCare, making it the safest choice while a phone is still covered. Independent repairers are often quicker to book and more flexible on price for out-of-warranty phones, and many use quality aftermarket parts that perform very close to genuine, though quality can vary between businesses.

sections.heading: What affects the cost of an iPhone repair?
sections.html: The model is the biggest factor, since parts for the newest iPhones are priced very differently from older or more common models. Whether the part is genuine or aftermarket changes the price too, as does any additional damage beyond the obvious fault, such as water exposure affecting multiple components. Because of how much this varies, it's worth checking a current, itemised price list for your exact iPhone model rather than relying on a number you've seen for a different device.

sections.heading: Preparing your iPhone for repair
sections.html: Back up your iPhone to iCloud or a computer before handing it over, and turn off Find My iPhone under your Apple ID settings — Activation Lock can prevent a repairer from properly testing the device once the repair is complete. It's also worth noting your passcode in case functionality testing requires it, though a reputable repairer should only need what's strictly necessary.

sections.heading: Warranty expectations for an iPhone repair
sections.html: Whichever option you choose, ask what warranty applies to the specific repair and how long it lasts. Apple-authorised repairs typically carry a standard warranty period on the part and workmanship, and independent repairers should offer something comparable in writing. If the same fault reappears shortly after the repair, a clear warranty is what protects you from paying twice.

faq.q: Will a non-Apple screen trigger a warning message?
faq.a: Yes, iOS can display a notice that it's unable to verify a part is genuine after certain repairs, though this doesn't prevent the phone from working normally.

faq.q: Does a third-party battery affect battery health reporting?
faq.a: It can — the battery health percentage relies on calibration tied to genuine Apple components, so a non-genuine battery may show a less accurate or unavailable reading.

faq.q: How long does an iPhone screen repair take?
faq.a: With the part in stock, most iPhone screen repairs are completed within a few hours to a day; less common models can take longer if a part needs to be ordered in.

faq.q: Do I need to turn off Find My iPhone before a repair?
faq.a: Yes — turning off Find My iPhone and signing out of your Apple ID where required prevents Activation Lock from blocking the repairer's ability to fully test the device afterward.
